title: Rapino and Leiweke Discuss Outbidding SeatGeek for a Major Venue Deal
documentTitle: United States v. Live Nation Entertainment & Ticketmaster — Exhibit PX0076
excerptForBlog:
On Feb 27, 2021, Tim Leiweke wrote to Michael Rapino and Irving Azoff: "Three bids, u, sg, axs. Your $6 million behind. You don't need them. We are going to take most of their music. Lousy union deals and bad loud in out."

Rapino replied: "Yes they want all the secondary money that seatgeek offering them. We tried many time to tell them can't give them 90% on secondary because the artist has to approve and if they do approve we want to play the artist so taking 90 from seatgeek sounds like 6 million but no artist will ever approve it so they won't ever actually get the money."

sourceCase: United States v. Live Nation Entertainment, Inc. & Ticketmaster L.L.C.
artifactNote: On February 27, 2021, Oak View Group CEO Tim Leiweke messaged Live Nation CEO Michael Rapino and Irving Azoff about a venue ticketing contract with three competing bids — Ticketmaster, SeatGeek, and AXS — noting Live Nation was trailing by $6 million. Rapino's reply explains his view of why SeatGeek's offer of roughly 90% secondary-market revenue to the venue was, in his assessment, unlikely to materialize in practice because artist approval would be required. The exchange became Plaintiff's Exhibit PX0076 in United States v. Live Nation Entertainment & Ticketmaster (S.D.N.Y., filed 2024), the DOJ-led antitrust case that put Live Nation's competitive conduct under federal scrutiny, making this a firsthand record of how its leadership discussed rivals during the period covered by the government's allegations.
lessonTitle: Rapino and Leiweke Discuss Outbidding SeatGeek for a Major Venue Deal
pullQuote: A candid 2021 exchange between Live Nation's CEO and a major venue operator, later entered into evidence in the DOJ's antitrust suit, offers a rare window into how Ticketmaster's executives framed competitive pressure from rival ticketing platforms.
